newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - March 10.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- The ruling New Korea Party has suggested to the presidential Blue House that it would be helpful if President Kim Young-sam's son, Kim Hyun-chul, testified before the National Assembly about his role in the Hanbo scandal.
- The Education Ministry plans to implement more flexible curriculums for elementary, middle and high school students, effective 2000.
- Lee Han-dong, a member of parliamentary and an advisor to the ruling New Korea Party, is considering giving up his desire to run for the December presidential elections, a source close to Lee said.
- Ex-Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung said he would not join the ruling New Korea Party.
- South Korea's ruling and opposition parties agreed on a revision bill of a controversial new labour law.

- South Korea's ruling and opposition parties, having struck a deal on amendments to the labour law over the weekend, will hold another round of negotiations today to remove the last stumbling block to the parliamentary passage of the bills.

- Secretary Hwang Jang-yop of North Korea's ruling Workers' Party, seeking asylum at the South Korean mission in Beijing, will be able to depart the Chinese capital in several days to come to Seoul via a third country, a government source said.
